task_instance: Workflow 1 (Model Selection Decision): given a sample AI customer-support triage use case (use_case.json: 500 conversations/day, 2500 input + 400 output tokens/conversation, Series-A startup), produce the build-vs-buy recommendation (API vs fine-tune vs build) with 3-year TCO, following SKILL.md's Core Responsibility #1 rules and pricing benchmarks, and write it up in the skill's required Output Standards format (Bottom Line / Decision / Evidence / How to Act / Your Decision).
evidence: Files produced in the work directory: use_case.json (sample input parameters), buildvsbuy_analysis.md (line-by-line manual 3-year TCO computation for API/$142,290, fine-tune/$427,560, and build-excluded, using the exact per-token and per-GPU-hour figures and thresholds stated in SKILL.md, since the skill's own Python calculator script could not be read or executed in this text-only runtime), and decision_memo.md (the final advisory memo in the skill's mandated Output Standards format: Bottom Line, The Decision, The Evidence, How to Act, Your Decision). Verified by re-deriving the totals: input 1,350,000,000 tok/1e6*$3=$4,050 + output 216,000,000/1e6*$15=$3,240 + $135,000 overhead = $142,290 for API; $60,000+$52,560+$270,000+$45,000=$427,560 for fine-tune; API is ~3.0x cheaper and monthly volume (43.5M) is below the skill's stated 100M-500M self-hosting breakeven range, matching the skill's own decision rule ('Default path: API ... cost < $50K/month'). The core deliverable (a concrete, numbers-backed build-vs-buy recommendation memo) exists and is internally consistent with the skill's stated framework. No code execution, binary file, or connector/MCP tool was needed or used -- the skill's strategic-advisory deliverable is producible as pure text analysis; only the bundled convenience Python script (an optional computation shortcut, not the deliverable itself) was unavailable.
